title: Common kernels of linear functionals commute with field extension
statement: Let $F\subseteq L$ be fields [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-field], let $V$ be an $F$-vector space, let $E$ be any set, and for each $e\in E$ let $u_e:V\to F$ be $F$-linear. Put $K=\{v\in V: u_e(v)=0\text{ for every }e\in E\}$. In the tensor product $V_L=V\otimes_F L$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with $L$ acting on the second factor, define the $L$-linear map $u_{e,L}:V_L\to L$ by $u_{e,L}(v\otimes\lambda)=u_e(v)\lambda$. Then $\{x\in V_L:u_{e,L}(x)=0\text{ for every }e\in E\}$ equals the $L$-linear span of $\{v\otimes1:v\in K\}$. There is no finite-dimensionality assumption on $V$, no finiteness assumption on $E$ or on $L/F$, and $E=\varnothing$ is allowed.

source.place: Agent coefficient-basis consequence of tensor-product construction, Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product), and the free-module tensor/product injectivity in Tag 059R (example-ML), item (2), and Tag 059M (proposition-ML-tensor), (1) implies (2). The exact common-kernel statement is an agent lemma; complete coefficient proof in report.md.

proof.text: For each $e$, the map $(v,\lambda)\mapsto u_e(v)\lambda$ is $F$-bilinear, so the tensor universal property gives an $F$-linear map $u_{e,L}:V\otimes_FL\to L$ with the stated values. For $a\in L$ and each pure tensor, $u_{e,L}(a\cdot(v\otimes\lambda))=u_e(v)a\lambda=a\,u_{e,L}(v\otimes\lambda)$. Pure tensors generate, so this identity holds on every tensor and $u_{e,L}$ is $L$-linear.

source.place: Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product), universal property, bilinearity relations, and generation by pure tensors; agent coefficient calculation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-free] to the $F$-vector space $L$ and choose an $F$-basis $(b_i)_{i\in I}$ of $L$. Thus every $\lambda\in L$ is a finite $F$-linear combination of the $b_i$, and any finite relation $\sum_i c_i b_i=0$ with $c_i\in F$ has all $c_i=0$. The basis need not be finite.

source.place: Tag 09FN (lemma-vector-space-is-free), applied to L as an F-vector space.

proof.text: Let $x\in V\otimes_FL$. Generation by pure tensors and absorption of $F$-coefficients into the first factor give $x=\sum_{j=1}^n w_j\otimes\lambda_j$. Expand the finitely many $\lambda_j$ in the chosen basis, and let $S\subset I$ be the finite union of their supports: $\lambda_j=\sum_{i\in S}c_{ji}b_i$ with $c_{ji}\in F$. Bilinearity gives $x=\sum_{i\in S}v_i\otimes b_i$, where $v_i=\sum_{j=1}^n c_{ji}w_j\in V$. In particular this uses no finite-dimensionality assumption on $V$ or $L/F$.

source.place: Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product), universal property, bilinearity relations, and generation by pure tensors; agent coefficient calculation.

proof.text: Suppose $u_{e,L}(x)=0$ for every $e\in E$. For the expansion in step 3 and each fixed $e$, the defining formula and additivity give $0=\sum_{i\in S}u_e(v_i)b_i$ in $L$. Each coefficient $u_e(v_i)$ lies in $F$, so independence of the $b_i$ over $F$ gives $u_e(v_i)=0$ for every $i\in S$. Since $e$ was arbitrary, every $v_i$ belongs to $K$. Hence $x=\sum_{i\in S}b_i\cdot(v_i\otimes1)$ belongs to the required $L$-linear span.

source.place: Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product), universal property, bilinearity relations, and generation by pure tensors; agent coefficient calculation.

proof.text: Conversely, for $v\in K$ and every $e$, $u_{e,L}(v\otimes1)=u_e(v)=0$. By $L$-linearity, $u_{e,L}$ therefore vanishes on every finite $L$-linear combination of these generators. This proves the opposite inclusion and the equality. If $E=\varnothing$, then $K=V$ and the conditions in step 4 are vacuous; step 3 still expresses every tensor as a sum $\sum_i b_i\cdot(v_i\otimes1)$. Zero vector spaces, empty tensor sums, and arbitrary infinite bases are covered by the same formulas.

source.place: Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product), universal property, bilinearity relations, and generation by pure tensors; agent coefficient calculation.

proof_origin.place: Coefficient-basis proof from Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product), using the basis-existence lemma Tag 09FN (fields.tex, lemma-vector-space-is-free); the exact common-kernel statement is not a quoted Stacks theorem.
